:::{#exr-basis-unique-practice}
#### Counting the ways to write a vector in a basis

@thm-basis-unique is what makes [coordinates](#def-coordinates) well defined.
The vectors $\vecf{a}_1 = \tp{(1, 1)}$ and $\vecf{a}_2 = \tp{(1, -1)}$ form a [basis](#def-basis) of $\reals^2$,
and

$$
\sbmat{5 \\ 1} = 3 \vecf{a}_1 + 2 \vecf{a}_2.
$$

How many lists of numbers $c_1, c_2$ satisfy $\tp{(5, 1)} = c_1 \vecf{a}_1 + c_2 \vecf{a}_2$?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Use @thm-basis-unique.
